cases.name: package-versus-analysis-choice
cases.description: The layout follows the artifact's contract instead of applying package scaffolding everywhere.
cases.prompt: A team has reusable data-cleaning functions, tests, two reports, and a scheduled analysis. Recommend a project layout and explain which code belongs in a package versus report scripts.
traps: The model puts all logic in report chunks or creates a package with no separation for report-specific execution.

assertions.text: Recommends placing reusable functions in R/ or a package source boundary.
Keeps reports separate from reusable logic.
Includes a tests/testthat/ boundary for reusable code.
Explains why the mixed project is appropriate.

cases.name: generated-package-files
cases.description: The answer respects roxygen2-generated package artifacts.
cases.prompt: A contributor manually edited NAMESPACE and a .Rd file to fix a package check. What should the project workflow do instead?
traps: The model recommends continuing to hand-edit generated files.

assertions.text: Recommends changing roxygen2 source comments or DESCRIPTION instead of hand-editing generated files.
Mentions running documentation generation and checking the resulting diff.
Identifies NAMESPACE and .Rd files as generated artifacts in the usual roxygen2 workflow.

cases.name: reproducible-analysis-paths
cases.description: The solution avoids machine-specific working-directory assumptions.
cases.prompt: Review an R Markdown report that begins with `setwd('/Users/alice/project')` and reads `../data/final.csv`. Make it runnable for CI and another analyst.
traps: The model only changes the absolute path to another hard-coded path.

assertions.text: Uses project-root-relative path resolution such as here::here() or an explicit root parameter.
Makes inputs and output destinations visible and reproducible.
